notes.text: Requires EasyApache 4 and the WebServer role; INI operations additionally require MultiPHP enabled. Requests act through the selected account.
Values use directive:value strings. Multiple values use directive, directive-1, and so on. Directive values are sensitive and are form encoded in POST; the operation declares no rollback.

The pinned data schema is unconstrained: preserve any present JSON payload, including null, false, zero or opaque objects. An absent data member is a mismatch; this method does not discard the response.

evidence.note: Pinned /LangPHP/php_ini_set_user_content has x-readonly=false and x-rollback=none. The data schema is a nullable object although the prose says always null; retain nullable opaque object validation.

notes.text: Requires EasyApache 4 and the WebServer role; INI operations additionally require MultiPHP enabled. Requests act through the selected account.

Replaces the selected INI content; there is no rollback. The client form-encodes the supplied content once. The pinned example is percent-encoded, and the server write/read round trip remains unverified. The content argument is sensitive; empty text is sent rather than omitted.
The pinned type description says home/vhost while its enum says host/vhost. This discrepancy is not silently resolved; the method forwards the supplied string. With type=vhost, supply vhost.
The response prose says always null, but its schema permits a nullable object. Preserve null or opaque object fields; absent data remains a mismatch.
